Let $T_{r} = \frac{(2r-1)(2r+1)(2r+3)(2r+5)}{64}$, then
$\lim_{n \to \infty} \sum_{r=1}^{n} \frac{1}{T_{r}}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$T_{r} = \frac{(2r-1)(2r+1)(2r+3)(2r+5)}{64}$
$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{T_{r}} = \frac{64}{16\left(r - \frac{1}{2}\right)\left(r + \frac{1}{2}\right)\left(r + \frac{3}{2}\right)\left(r + \frac{5}{2}\right)}$
$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{T_{r}} = \frac{\frac{4}{3}\left[\left(r + \frac{5}{2}\right) - \left(r - \frac{1}{2}\right)\right]}{\left(r - \frac{1}{2}\right)\left(r + \frac{1}{2}\right)\left(r + \frac{3}{2}\right)\left(r + \frac{5}{2}\right)}$
$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{T_{r}} = \frac{4}{3}\left[\frac{1}{\left(r - \frac{1}{2}\right)\left(r + \frac{1}{2}\right)\left(r - \frac{3}{2}\right)} - \frac{1}{\left(r + \frac{1}{2}\right)\left(r + \frac{3}{2}\right)\left(r + \frac{5}{2}\right)}\right]$
$\lim_{n \to \infty} \sum_{r=1}^{n} \frac{1}{T_{r}} = \frac{4}{3}\left[\frac{1}{\frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{3}{2} \cdot \frac{5}{2}} - \frac{1}{\frac{3}{2} \cdot \frac{5}{2} \cdot \frac{7}{2}}\right]$
$\frac{1}{\frac{3}{2} \cdot \frac{5}{2} \cdot \frac{7}{2}} - \frac{1}{\frac{5}{2} \cdot \frac{7}{2} \cdot \frac{9}{2}}$
$= \frac{4}{3}\left[\frac{8}{15}\right] = \frac{32}{45}$

questions.stem: If the images of the points $A(1, 3)$, $B(3, 1)$ and $C(2, 4)$ in the line $x + 2y = 4$ are D, E and F respectively, then the centroid of the triangle DEF is
questions.solution:
Centroid of the $\Delta DEF$ is the mirror image of the centroid of the $\Delta ABC$ about the line $x + 2y = 4$.
$G_{1}$ = Centroid of $\Delta ABC \equiv (2, 3)$, $G_{2} \equiv$ Centroid of $\Delta DEF$.
[Figure: $G_{1}(2, 3)$, foot $M\left(\frac{x_{1}+2}{2}, \frac{y_{1}+3}{2}\right)$ on $x + 2y = 4$, $G_{2}(x_{1}, y_{1})$]
$\Rightarrow \frac{y_{1} - 3}{x_{1} - 2} = 2,\ \frac{x_{1} + 2}{2} + (y_{1} + 3) = 4$
$\Rightarrow x_{1} = \frac{2}{5},\ y_{1} = -\frac{1}{5}$
$\Rightarrow G_{2} = \left(\frac{2}{5}, -\frac{1}{5}\right)$

questions.stem: Let $|Z_{i}| = 1$ for $i = 1, 2, 3$ satisfying $\left|\bar{Z}_{1}Z_{2} + \bar{Z}_{2}Z_{3} + \bar{Z}_{3}Z_{1}\right|^{2} = a + b\sqrt{2}$, where a, b an rational numbers such that $\arg(Z_{1}) = \frac{\pi}{4},\ \arg(Z_{2}) = 0$ and $\arg(Z_{3}) = \frac{-\pi}{4}$, then find (a, b)
questions.solution:
$Z_{1} = |1|\,e^{i\frac{\pi}{4}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} + i \cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$
$Z_{2} = |1|\,e^{-(0)}1 + 0i$
$Z_{3} = |1|\,e^{-i\frac{\pi}{4}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} - \frac{i}{\sqrt{2}}$
$\bar{Z}_{1}Z_{2} = \left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} - \frac{i}{\sqrt{2}}\right)(1)$
$\bar{Z}_{2}Z_{3} = 1\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} - \frac{i}{\sqrt{2}}\right)$
$\bar{Z}_{3}Z_{1} = \left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} + \frac{i}{\sqrt{2}}\right)\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} + \frac{i}{\sqrt{2}}\right)$
$\Rightarrow \bar{Z}_{1}Z_{2} + \bar{Z}_{2}Z_{3} + \bar{Z}_{3}Z_{1} = \left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} - \frac{i}{\sqrt{2}}\right) + \left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} - \frac{i}{\sqrt{2}}\right) + \left(\frac{1}{2} - \frac{1}{2}\right) + 2i\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)$
$= \sqrt{2} - \sqrt{2}i + i$
$\Rightarrow \left|\bar{Z}_{1}Z_{2} + \bar{Z}_{2}Z_{3} + \bar{Z}_{3}Z_{1}\right|^{2} = \left|\sqrt{2} + i\left(-\sqrt{2} + 1\right)\right|^{2}$
$= \left(\sqrt{\left(\sqrt{2}\right)^{2} + \left(1 - \sqrt{2}\right)^{2}}\right)^{2}$
$= 5 - 2\sqrt{2}$
$(a, b) = (5, -2)$

questions.stem: Let $\vec{b} = \lambda\hat{i} + 4\hat{k}, \lambda > 0$ and the projection vector of $\vec{b}$ on $\vec{a} = 2\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - \hat{k}$ is $\vec{c}$. If $|\vec{a} + \vec{c}| = 7$, then the area of the parallelogram formed by vector $\vec{b}$ and $\vec{c}$ is (in square units)
questions.solution:
$\vec{c} = (\vec{b} \cdot \hat{a})\hat{a} = \frac{2\lambda - 4}{6}\vec{a}$
$\because\ |\vec{a} + \vec{c}| = 7 \Rightarrow \left|\vec{a}\left(1 + \frac{2\lambda - 4}{9}\right)\right| = 7$
$\left|\frac{5 + 2\lambda}{9}\right| \times 3 = 7 \Rightarrow |5 + 2\lambda| = 21$
$\because\ \lambda > 0 \Rightarrow \lambda = 8$
$\Rightarrow \vec{c} = \frac{4}{3}\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b} = 4(2\hat{i} - \hat{k})$
$\Rightarrow \vec{b} \times \vec{c} = \frac{16}{3}\begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 2 & 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 2 & -1 \end{vmatrix} = \frac{16}{3}(-2\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + 4\hat{k})$
$\Rightarrow \left|\vec{b} \times \vec{c}\right| = \frac{32}{3}|-\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}| = 32$
$\Rightarrow$ Area of parallelogram formed by $\vec{b}$ and $\vec{c}$
$\Rightarrow \left|\vec{b} \times \vec{c}\right| = 32$

If A be a $3 \times 3$ square matrix such that $\det(A) = -2$. If $\det(3\,\mathrm{adj}(-6\,\mathrm{adj}(3A)) = 2^{n} \cdot 3^{m}$, where $m \ge n$, then $4m + 2n$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Concept: $A.\,\mathrm{adj}(A) = |A|I$, $\det(\lambda A) = \lambda^{n}\det(A)$
$\Rightarrow \det(A) = |A|^{n-1}$, where n is order
$\Rightarrow \det(3\,\mathrm{adj}(-6\,\mathrm{adj}(3A)))$
$= 3^{3} \cdot \det(\mathrm{adj}(-6\,\mathrm{adj}(3A)))$
$= 3^{3} \cdot (-6\,\mathrm{adj}(3A)))^{2}$
$= 3^{3} \cdot (-6)^{6}\,|3A|^{4}$
$= 3^{9} \cdot 2^{6} \cdot 3^{12} \cdot (-2)^{4}$
$= 3^{21} \cdot 2^{10}$
$\therefore\ n = 10, m = 21$
$\therefore\ 4m + 2n = 104$
